findings.title: An account launch whose collateral can't come back as an output: no test fails without the refusal
findings.scenario: The public account launches a pool (launch_from_account, the web wallet's buildAccountLaunch at wasm lib.rs:2601) with a collateral too small to cover 3/2 of the fee and still come back as an output. The collateral is either the one the wallet set aside (request.collateral) or one picked by account_collateral (build.rs:3824), which sorts the available UTxOs but never filters them. With the check, the launch is refused in words: "The public account's collateral is too small to put up for this launch". With it removed, on preprod's parameters and default terms, a 1 ₳ collateral gives a built and measured launch with a fee of 0.428774 ₳ and a collateral return of 0.356839 ₳ (1.2 ₳ gives 0.556839 ₳). Both are under the least an ADA-only output there holds (about 0.98 ₳), so the node refuses the signed launch at submit. No funds move; the user gets the node's error instead of the wallet's words.

findings.title: A cancel's collateral holding a token or a datum: no test fails without the refusal
findings.scenario: cancel_orders is handed a collateral row that holds a token, an inline datum or a datum hash. Anyone can send such a UTxO to the session's address. With the check, the cancel is refused: "The session's collateral must hold ADA alone". With it removed, the cancel builds and measures, but its collateral return is ADA alone (`Output::new(c.address.clone(), back)`, orders.rs:1030). On the MinswapV2 mainnet fixture: fee 0.236014 ₳, collateral return 4.645979 ₳ with no token. The ledger refuses that cancel after the session signs it, because a collateral's tokens must come back in its return. With a datum instead, the cancel builds and the ledger takes it. Today nothing reaches this check: the worker only ever puts up a 5 ₳ row of ADA alone or a plainAda row as collateral (sessions.ts:1052 collateralFits, :1081 plainAda, :4218-4219 cancelOf). This check backs that TypeScript filter up.

findings.title: A cancel built on a datum other than the one its order holds: no test fails without the check
findings.scenario: The datum bytes in OrderToCancel don't match the order: they differ from its inline datum, or don't hash to its datum hash, or the order holds no datum at all. With the check, each case is refused in words. With all three arms removed: (1) an inline order given its datum in other bytes (the same data, its field list re-encoded) builds a cancel (fee 0.236014 ₳), so ownership was decided on bytes the order's script never sees; (2) an order by hash given other bytes is refused by the evaluator ("missing required datum"); (3) an order holding no datum is refused by the evaluator ("missing required inline datum or datum hash in script input"). In every case the order's own script runs on its real datum, and everything goes back to the session, so nothing pays elsewhere. Nothing reaches the check today: the worker takes the bytes from the row's inline datum or from Koios's datum_info for its hash (sessions.ts cancelOf, a trusted source), and check_cancels takes them from the swap's own bytes (order_at).

Then I ran `--test orders_test` (26 passed) and `--lib --tests` (356 passed). The combined seedelf-wasm run also passed (305). Every test's OrderToCancel takes the datum its row holds: Setup::order, and with_datum at orders_test.rs:631 keeps the row and the bytes in step. findings.title: A cancel spending a session row that holds a datum or a script: no test fails without the refusal
findings.scenario: One of the session's funds rows holds an inline datum, a datum hash or a reference script: a stranger's UTxO at the session's address. With the check, the cancel is refused: "holds a datum or a script, so a cancel can't spend it". With it removed, a row with an inline datum or a datum hash gets spent into the cancel (built, fee 0.236014 ₳). The ledger takes that, since key-locked inputs need no datum, and the row's ADA comes back with the change. A row with a reference script is still refused, but in eval::resolve_row's words ("holds a reference script, which the wallet can't evaluate with yet"). Nothing reaches the check today: the worker passes only plainAda rows as funds (sessions.ts:4218, :4234).

findings.title: A reference holding two lovejoin NFTs, or its policy's one token under another name: no test fails without the check
findings.scenario: A reference UTxO at the holder holds the genuine pool policy's token in quantity 2, or holds one token of that policy not named lovejoin. With the check, verify_pool refuses it as Rejected::NotOneNft. With the quantity half removed, or the name half, verify_pool trusts it. No chain can hold either: one_shot_mint mints exactly one token, named lovejoin, in a single event (Lovejoin 29573c5 validators/one_shot_mint.ak pins `asset_name == #"6c6f76656a6f696e"` and `quantity == 1`), and a token under any other policy is refused as WrongSeed. So only a reference made up offline reaches the check, and the ledger refuses any transaction that reads a UTxO that doesn't exist. The existing NotOneNft case (lovejoin_pools_test.rs:507) adds an asset under another policy, which the one-policy pattern at :312 refuses.

findings.title: A v2 pool whose datum names another mix_logic: no test fails without the L check
findings.scenario: A pool-launcher launches on the v2 set with a datum naming v2's M and F but another L′; one_shot_mint never checks the three hashes. derive_for(seed, L′) matches neither set, so it falls back to v2 (templates.rs:179-191). M then matches, because v2's M is applied over v2's own L. So only pool.rs:415 refuses this pool, as WrongScripts. With that line removed, the wallet trusts and shows the pool. Its mixes would still run: the wallet builds from the derived scripts, mix_box takes L as its parameter, and mix_logic reads only M from the datum. The only on-chain reader of the datum's L is fee_contract, which the wallet never uses. So the harm is a pool shown that the wallet's own rule says isn't genuine. The existing wrong-L case (lovejoin_pools_test.rs:485-494) uses the TokenV1 preprod fixture, where v2's M differs from the datum's, so the M check at :414 refuses it first. That case pinned :415 until 41b7ca8c replaced `templates::derive` (the V1 set alone) with `derive_for`.
findings.since: The check came in 4550b9ef (2026-10-17, chunk 34a; web-wallet/1.6.0). Its only pin was lost in 41b7ca8c (2026-11-05, chunk 44a; first tag web-wallet/1.8.0).

findings.title: A finished launch that isn't the pool meant: no test fails without launched_pool's checks
findings.scenario: launched_pool is the last check before the web wallet signs a launch (wasm lib.rs:2611, :2702). It verifies the pool in the finished bytes (:699) and that both scripts are read from the holder (:701). Every test feeds it a launch the wallet just built with its own seed, which passes both checks by construction. With :701 removed, Lovejoin's own preprod launch, whose scripts sit at a key address, reads back as a launch to sign (the probe gets Ok). With :699's verify_pool replaced by the same derivation without its checks, a launch read back under a seed it didn't spend is still refused, but only by :701, in its words: "The launch doesn't publish its scripts at the holder". A launch whose outputs held its seed's scripts at the holder beside a datum or NFT that isn't that seed's would be signed. Only a construction bug in the wallet's own builder reaches either check.

findings.title: The bundled order table's load checks: no test fails without them, and as written none can
findings.scenario: table() refuses three kinds of bad row in the bundled orders.json: a carried Plutus V1 script that isn't its row's pinned hash (:225), a row with no place or two places to read its script from (:231), and a carried script that isn't V1 (:234). The bundled file is right today, so with each check removed it still loads and every test passes. table()'s only input is the bundled file (`const TABLE: &str = include_str!("orders.json")`, :56), so no test can hand it a bad row. If orders.json were edited wrongly, these checks would refuse the table at load, and every cancel would fail in words, instead of cancels going out carrying a script the ledger rejects. The table test (orders_test.rs:212) checks that only V1 rows are carried (`e.inline.is_some() == (e.plutus == 1)`), not their hashes.
findings.since: aef01f72 (2026-10-07); first tag containing it web-wallet/1.6.0
findings.evidence: Changes, in my copy only, each applied alone: orders.rs:225 `if false && script_hash(row.plutus, &bytes) != script`, :231 `if false && reference.is_none() == inline.is_none()`, :234 `if false && inline.is_some() && row.plutus != 1`. For each, `cargo test -p seedelf-core --lib --test orders_test` passed (28). Nothing else in seedelf-core reaches orders.rs: grep finds `orders` only in orders.rs, lib.rs's `pub mod orders`, and tests/orders_test.rs. g20a's first try also passed the orders_test file alone, before I stopped its crate phase. All three together passed in the combined seedelf-wasm run (305).
findings.fix: Split table() into `table_from(json: &str, network_flag: bool)`, keeping `table(f) = table_from(TABLE, f)`. Then test, each refused in words: a row whose carried script doesn't hash to its `script`, a row with both `reference` and `inline` and one with neither, and a carried script on a Plutus V2 row.

findings.title: A cancel declaring less than its finished bytes measure: no test fails without the check
findings.scenario: build_cancel measures a draft and settles the fee from it. It then measures the finished cancel and returns it only if the draft's budgets cover what the finished one uses; otherwise it retries with a 1% margin. With the check replaced by `true`, every test passes. In every fixture the first pass's budgets already cover the finished cancel: several_orders_of_one_plutus_version_cancel_in_one_transaction re-evaluates each built cancel and asserts eval::declared_covers. So the retry is never reached in any test. If a DEX script's cost moved with the fee or the declared budgets (the case the retry's comment describes: "used a hair more than the draft's"), the cancel would go out declaring less than it uses, and the node would refuse it in phase two after the user signed Stop's cancel.
findings.since: aef01f72 (2026-10-07); first tag containing it web-wallet/1.6.0
findings.evidence: Change, in my copy only, at orders.rs:1102-1106: `if budgets.iter().zip(&used).all(|(ours, theirs)| ours.mem >= theirs.mem && ours.steps >= theirs.steps) {` became `if true {`, so the first pass always returns. `cargo test -p seedelf-core --lib --test orders_test` passed (28), including the eval::declared_covers assertion near orders_test.rs:978. The combined seedelf-wasm run passed too (305), including session_test's own cancels of the order fixtures.
findings.fix: Give the settle loop a seam a test can drive. For example, factor the acceptance into `fn covers(ours: &[Budget], theirs: &[Budget]) -> bool` with a unit test at its boundary (equal passes, one unit short of mem or steps fails), and let build_cancel take its first budgets in a lib test (orders.rs's tests module), seeded 1% under what the draft measures. Then assert that the cancel returned after the second pass declares budgets that cover a fresh evaluation (eval::declared_covers).

notes: Merged duplicates: R3b lists 30 guards and none repeats. Several entries hold more than one check, so I split them into 84 mutants, one per check (the `guards` list gives each line).

Mutants no test can catch, which I don't count as findings. pool.rs:177 (box_lovelace > 0) is implied by 0 < max_fee < box_lovelace at :183. orders.rs:309 `!order.pays.is_empty()` can't be false: every OrderRead comes from read() (orders.rs:574), and every arm names a payee; the only callers are cancel_orders:776 and wasm lib.rs:735. launch.rs:239 (verify_derived) and :247 (inline scripts) self-check outputs that shaped() builds from the same derived scripts, so no input through the public API reaches them.

launch.rs:168, check_terms' 10 ₳ arm: removed alone, nothing fails, because verify_derived's AdaPool refuses the same launch in words that still contain 'copy of the classic pool'. With :239 removed too, the launch is built, and launched_pool refuses it: "The launch makes no reference UTxO the wallet would read". That fails the wasm test lovejoin_flows_test.rs an_ada_pool_starts_from_the_seedelf_balance (:771), as my first combined run showed. So the 10 ₳ refusal has two layers, and only the pair is pinned.

Caught, but not by the test the lane named. pool.rs:449 is caught by the_wallet_trusts_lovejoins_preprod_pool, not :905. pool.rs:158, :170, :189, :194 and :142 are caught only by lovejoin_vectors_test.rs (the vectors shared with the data layer), not by :649. launch.rs:406 is caught only by the lib test's count of measures: no test launches an unusable pool through launch_apart, the path the web wallet's private launch takes (wasm lib.rs:2692). orders.rs:444 is caught by a native stack overflow that aborts the whole orders_test binary, which loses the other tests' results when it fires.

Guards 21 and 24 back up TypeScript filters: the worker's collateralFits (sessions.ts:1052) and plainAda (:1081, used by cancelOf at :4218-4219) keep a stranger's rows out before WebAssembly sees them. Whether a Vitest test pins those filters is for a TypeScript lens; I didn't try it.

build.rs:3747, the account mint's collateral-return check, has the same shape as t1d#1. Its words appear in no test (grep of seedelf-core/tests, wasm/tests and extension/tests). I didn't mutate it: it isn't on R3b's list.

The extension's Vitest tests reach these Rust guards only through TREE's prebuilt wasm/pkg, which a Rust mutant can't change, so I didn't run them (as the brief says). seedelf-cli doesn't call orders, launch or pool code (grep: 0 files).

seedelf-wasm's native suite (16 targets, 305 tests), run twice with every survivor applied together. First run, with launch.rs:168 included: 304 passed, 1 failed (the pair above). Second run, with every survivor except launch.rs:168: 305 passed. Its lovejoin_proven_bytes_test includes four script hex files from seedelf-verification/, outside seedelf-platform; I copied just those files (data, nothing built) into my second copy.

Each probe test in the findings' `fix` was appended to a second copy's test files. All 8 pass on the real code, and each fails under its mutant (9 probe-and-mutant runs). Results and probe logs are kept in SCRATCH/r51/work/T1d/results/ (tmpfs).

Interruption: to save time, I stopped the batch runner with SIGINT during g20a's crate phase. Its `finally` restored orders.rs; I stopped the one orphaned test binary (mine, checked by its CARGO_TARGET_DIR) and confirmed by cmp that every copy matched TREE. I then ran the last 11 orders.rs mutants with `--lib --test orders_test`, which is all of seedelf-core that reaches orders.rs.
The machine's load average was 23 to 68 throughout (other lanes), so crate phases took 1 to 9 minutes each. Timings in the logs reflect that.
coverage: I tried all 30 of R3b's guards (none repeats), as 84 mutants, each of a different check. 78 of them ran one at a time in my copy of seedelf-platform. Each ran its named test file first, then, if nothing failed, the whole seedelf-core crate (--lib --tests: 31 targets, 356 tests, 6 ignored). The exception is the last 11 orders.rs mutants, which ran --lib plus orders_test only (28 tests), since nothing else in the crate reaches orders.rs. Five more were never run apart, as their results are implied: g21's token and datum parts and g22's three arms, because removing each whole check failed nothing. g1de (the NFT's name and quantity together) ran only in the combined wasm runs. 27 checks that failed no seedelf-core test (the survivors and the equivalent ones) also ran in two combined runs of seedelf-wasm's native suite (305 tests); in the second, 305 passed. 9 probe tests (the tests a fix would add) ran in a second copy, at baseline and each under its mutant. Not run: the extension's Vitest tests (they reach these guards only through TREE's prebuilt wasm/pkg); seedelf-cli (it doesn't use these modules); live and ignored tests; Playwright. I didn't mutate guards outside R3b's list, such as build.rs:3747, ReferenceDatum::decode's own depth check at pool.rs:152, or orders.rs:1022's fee overflow check. Every copy, target directory and cache log of mine was removed at the end: $HOME/.cache/seedelf-review-51/T1d (with its probe copy), T1d-target, and my logs. TREE was never written (git diff of seedelf-core and wasm is empty).
